capabilities.target: calendar invite acceptance and prep note drafting

inputs.source: calendar invites including invites from outside the company; description is free text written by sender

instructions.note: The design gives the agent autonomous acceptance, document retrieval, and attendee emailing, with only a daily summary afterward and no structural restriction on recipients or document scope.
"find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees" does not define document scope, recipient trust, or data handling limits.

controls.name: Daily summary reviewed by executive after actions
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is generated by the same agent after acting; it does not block harmful actions and a more capable model can frame actions more persuasively or omit salient details.

controls.name: Recipient restriction bound to record for attendee email
Raw-action human approval gate for outbound attendee email
Scoped document access for calendar prep
Attributable tamper-evident action record for invite handling and outbound email

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite can drive confidential document retrieval and irreversible email egress to attendees

attack_path.note: Invite description is authored by anyone, including outside senders.
Prompt directs the agent to find related executive documents.
Prompt directs the agent to email a brief to attendees; runtime notes say any recipient, no approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

findings.residual_rationale: The only declared control is a post-action daily summary generated by the agent itself, which is detective and outside the credited preventive steps. Because no present structural or approval control constrains recipients, document scope, or outbound mail, the residual remains at the inherent level.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version change, rising task length, or any move from daily summary review toward less human scrutiny should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: The prompt tells the agent to accept each new invite, find related documents, and email a short brief to the attendees.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite, and the invite description is free text written by the sender.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, so the read step can access confidential data.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step.
The daily summary is written by the agent itself and occurs after actions are taken.

recommendations.action: Bind outbound email recipients to verified meeting attendees from the calendar record and block arbitrary recipient selection by the agent.
Require raw-action human approval before any outbound brief that leaves the trust boundary.
Restrict document retrieval for calendar prep to explicitly tagged prep materials or narrow folders instead of the executive's full drive.

findings.title: Identity and privilege abuse: the agent acts with the executive's mailbox and document access on instructions originating from untrusted invite content

attack_path.note: Agent reads documents under the executive's delegated access.
Agent sends from the executive's mailbox to attendees without approval.

findings.residual_rationale: No declared control narrows the executive-delegated credential use on either document reads or outbound email. The design therefore leaves the confused-deputy path fully reachable despite the post-action summary.

forecast.watch_signal: Any model swap, longer autonomous prep workflows, or reduced oversight leaves the executive-delegated authority equally exposed and should trigger reassessment.

evidence.observation: drive.search_and_read accesses the executive's documents, including board materials and draft financial results.
mail.send sends from the executive's mailbox to any recipient with no approval step.
The agent automatically acts on each new invite as it arrives.
Anyone can send an invite, so untrusted parties can influence actions carried out with the executive's own access.

recommendations.action: Replace broad executive-delegated search with a dedicated prep corpus or scoped service that excludes unrelated confidential files.
Require explicit authorization for outbound mail generated from invite-triggered workflows executed under the executive identity.

findings.title: Missing attributable action record for invite handling and outbound mail creates repudiation gaps on consequential actions
findings.residual_rationale: The artifacts mention only a daily summary authored by the agent, not a tamper-evident attributable action record that separates agent actions from the executive's own actions. Because no present control restores provenance, the property finding stays at the inherent floor.

forecast.watch_signal: If daily summaries are reduced further or autonomy rises, reviewers lose even the limited post hoc context now described.

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself.
The design describes no separate tamper-evident action log or attributable audit record for accepted invites or outbound email.
The agent takes consequential actions automatically and only reports later.

recommendations.action: Create tamper-evident per-action records that bind invite source, retrieved documents, recipients, payload, and whether the action was agent-initiated versus executive-initiated.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no spend capability, recursion, queue fan-out, or other availability-impacting action path to assess here.
The artifacts do not state whether invite sender identity is authenticated or whether spoofed calendar invitations are blocked upstream.
This assessment focuses on agent risk; no design facts describe any agent-managed nonrepudiation mechanism for outside senders themselves.
The inbound invite flow brings content into the agent but the disclosed harm in this design occurs on outbound mail, not on this ingress channel.
The artifacts do not describe invite rate limits, queueing, or overload behavior for calendar invite ingestion.
The artifacts say executive chat requests exist but do not describe the authentication method for that channel.
The artifacts do not state whether executive chat requests are recorded with attributable provenance separate from later agent actions.
The executive request flow is treated as the authenticated principal's own input, and no present finding depends on tampering of that flow.
This inbound trusted request flow is not itself an egress path and no evidence shows disclosure on that channel.
No artifact states queue limits, throttling, or abuse handling for the executive chat input channel.
The artifacts describe sensitive contents in the drive but do not state who can modify them or whether poisoning of prep documents is possible.
No artifact describes drive availability dependencies, quotas, or failure handling for retrieval during prep.
The artifacts do not state mail sending quotas, throttles, or retry behavior, so availability effects cannot be rated confidently.
The artifacts do not describe calendar integrity protections or whether malicious invite content can persistently alter event records beyond acceptance.
The described calendar capability accepts invites and drafts prep notes, but no evidence shows disclosure from the calendar store itself.
No artifact describes invite flood handling, calendar write quotas, or recovery controls for unwanted acceptances.
The design notes a daily summary exists but do not describe storage integrity, retention, or whether summaries can be altered after generation.
The artifacts do not state where summaries are stored, who can access them, or whether they contain confidential content.
The daily summary record is not described as a runtime dependency whose unavailability would block or amplify harmful actions.

rating.rationale: Present risk is critical because untrusted calendar invite content can directly reach confidential drive reads and irreversible outbound email from the executive's mailbox, with A3 autonomy and no structural recipient restriction, approval gate, or scoped prep corpus. Residual remains critical because the only declared control is an agent-written daily summary after actions complete, which is detective and earns no preventive tier credit. Forecast remains critical; the control most likely to decay first is ctrl.daily_summary, whose value further weakens under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, and autonomy_increase. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run in this environment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, runtime config, or audit schema was provided, so capability wiring, exact autonomy limits, and logging details were inferred from the prompt and runtime notes.
No line-numbered runtime artifact was supplied; evidence locators for runtime notes therefore cite the artifact name rather than exact lines.
Because upstream calendar authentication, attendee trust classification, and any hidden mail or drive controls were not provided, findings assume the documented unrestricted behavior is accurate.
